title: Applied ML: Quality Guardrails, Onboarding & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes the standardized process and guardrails used by the Applied ML team to onboard models into Redwood’s inference platform, create and maintain prompt sets and benchmarks, apply quantization profiles safely, and run regression triage when quality or cost regressions are detected. The goal is to enable fast model iteration while protecting customer-facing quality SLOs and ensuring reproducible, auditable decisions.

Audience: ML engineers, model owners, SREs, product managers, and evaluation reviewers.

Scope: Covers eval harness usage, prompt set and benchmark guidelines, model onboarding checklist, quantization profile validation, automated and manual regression triage workflows, and responsibilities. This playbook applies to hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment flows.

Key definitions
- Eval harness: The centralized test runner and CI integration we use to score models against labeled/heuristic test sets, including unit, integration, and scenario-level evaluations.
- Prompt set: A curated collection of inputs and expected behaviors used for automated evaluation and regression monitoring.
- Benchmark: An aggregated metric snapshot (accuracy, ROUGE, EM, factuality probe scores, hallucination rate, latency/cost) used to compare model variants.
- Guardrail: A policy (metric threshold, transformation rule, or rollout constraint) that prevents unsafe or unacceptable model behavior in production.

High-level workflow (summary)
1) Model proposal and initial evaluation
   - Model owner opens a Model Onboarding RFC with: model name/version, checkpoint source, intended use cases, expected token limits, and initial prompt examples.
   - Run baseline eval harness suite in sandbox (unit + scenario tests). Record metrics in the model-evals dashboard.
2) Prompt set & benchmark creation
   - Curate prompt sets (seeded from customer telemetry, fuzzing, and synthetic scenarios). Tag prompts with intent, difficulty, and failure modes.
   - Define benchmark targets (pass/fail thresholds) for each critical metric.
3) Quantization experiment and validation
   - Apply recommended quantization profile(s) from quant-profiles catalog. Run accuracy/regression tests and latency/cost profiling.
4) Pre-production rollout
   - Canary deploy to limited traffic with observational gating (quality checks + latency SLOs).
5) Regression monitoring & triage
   - Continuous evaluation on production prompt set stream and scheduled nightly re-runs. If a regression triggers, follow the regression triage playbook below.

Roles & responsibilities
- Model owner: primary contact for onboarding, triage, and mitigation plans.
- Applied ML evaluation lead: reviewer for prompt sets, benchmark definitions, and final gating sign-off.
- SRE/Platform: deploy canaries, collect latency/cost telemetry, and enforce rollout policies.
- QA/PM: review high-level user-impacting regressions and approve customer communications.

Eval harness standards
- Tests must be deterministic where possible and idempotent: seed RNGs, pin tokenizer versions, and freeze model weights for the run.
- Each test artifact must include: description, input file (CSV/JSONL), expected behavior, evaluation script, and evaluation metric(s).
- CI integration: every model PR must run the eval harness on a short smoke suite; merged changes must trigger full eval on the nightly runner.
- Naming convention: evals/{model-name}/{suite-name}/{YYYY-MM-DD}.jsonl for results.

Prompt sets and benchmarks guidelines
- Prompt set structure: each prompt entry must be annotated with fields: id, intent, source (telemetry | synthetic | third-party), difficulty (easy|medium|hard), and tags (safety|factuality|formatting).
- Minimum prompt set sizes: unit checks: 20 prompts; scenario benchmarks: 200 prompts; production monitoring sets: 500+ rolling samples.
- Benchmark metrics (examples): exact-match, BLEU/ROUGE, factuality-probe (model-self-consistency test), toxicity score (using internal classifier v2), hallucination flag rate, median latency @ p50/p95, and tokens-per-request cost estimate.
- Baseline thresholds: define required pass criteria per benchmark; e.g., scenario accuracy >= 87%, hallucination rate <= 3%, median latency <= 350ms for 1k tokens. Thresholds are set per product SLAs and documented in the benchmark manifest.

Model onboarding checklist (detailed)
1) Pre-eval: collect model metadata (architecture, tokenizer, checkpoint hash, training data provenance, license) and register in the model catalog.
2) Local eval: run unit tests and smoke-run on eval harness. Capture seed, tokenizer config, and hardware profile.
3) Prompt & benchmark creation: select prompt sets; run scenario benchmarks and capture metrics.
4) Quantization validation (if applicable): run quant profiles (4-bit/8-bit/FP16) and compare delta vs baseline on accuracy and hallucination metrics.
5) Canary & rollout plan: define canary percentage (default 2%), rollback triggers (quality drop > 4% absolute in critical metric or latency p95 increase > 30%), and monitoring windows.
6) Security & compliance checklist: verify PII redaction policies, KMS integration for Private deployments, and legal/licensing signoff.
7) Signoffs: Applied ML lead, Platform SRE, and Product SA.

Quantization profiles: best practices and validation matrix
- Start conservative: prefer FP16 -> 8-bit -> 4-bit. For each profile run:
   - Accuracy delta test: run core benchmarks and ensure no metric delta beyond agreed threshold (default: <= 2% abs for accuracy-type metrics; <= 1% absolute for hallucination-sensitive tasks).
   - Consistency tests: run 100 paired prompts with differing lengths to validate KV-cache behavior and output determinism.
   - Fallback policy: if profile fails key checks, automatically route to higher-precision variant in canary traffic.
- Keep a catalog (quantization-profiles.csv) with columns: profile_id, base_precision, expected_speedup, known_issues, owner, last_verified.

Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)
1) Detection
   - Automated alerts come from: nightly eval runs, production monitoring stream (rolling prompt-set scoring), and customer-reported incidents. Alert channels: PagerDuty and #applied-ml-alerts Slack.
2) Triage intake (first 30 minutes)
   - Assign incident owner (typically model owner). Collect: model id, deployment id, timeframe, metric deltas, and example failed prompts.
   - Quick dampening: if the regression magnitude is small and within statistical noise, label as "monitor" and schedule a deeper run.
3) Rapid root-cause hypotheses (30-90 minutes)
   - Check recent changes: model rollback/upgrade, prompt/template changes, tokenizer updates, quantization profile changes, or serving runtime updates (kernel/torch).
   - Run differential eval: baseline (previous stable) vs current on targeted prompt set and a random sample from production.
4) Mitigation (within 2 hours goal for customer-impacting regressions)
   - If regression is clearly caused by model variant or quantization: rollback to last known-good variant.
   - If caused by prompt/template changes: revert prompt change or apply prompt-specific safety wrappers.
   - If caused by serving/runtime change: apply traffic routing to an unaffected region/cluster and open infra ticket.
5) Root cause analysis (post-incident)
   - Produce a short RCA: timeline, contributing factors, corrective actions, and follow-ups. Attach eval artifacts (result JSONs), example failing prompts, and dashboard snapshots.
   - Update prompt sets/benchmarks and quantization profile catalog if needed.

Metrics, SLOs & alert thresholds (recommended defaults)
- Quality SLOs (per-route): scenario accuracy >= 90% (critical routes), hallucination rate <= 2% (critical), toxicity rate <= 0.5%.
- Latency SLOs: median latency <= 300ms (short-text routes), p95 <= 800ms.
- Cost guardrails: tokens-per-request increase vs baseline <= 12% during rollout.
- Alert thresholds: automatic alert if quality delta > 3% absolute on any critical route, or p95 latency increase > 25%.

Operational examples & CLI snippets
- Run a named benchmark locally:
  ./eval-harness run --suite=clarify-factuality --model=redwood-v2-7b --tokens=512 --out=results/redwood-v2-7b-clarity-20270210.json
- Compare two runs (diff tool):
  ./eval-harness diff --base=results/redwood-v2-7b-20270201.json --head=results/redwood-v2-7b-20270210.json --metrics=accuracy,hallucination
- Promote model with canary policy:
  deploy promote --model redwood-v2-7b --canary 2% --rollback-on quality_drop>4% --monitoring=eval-harness-nightly

Governance & documentation updates
- Every onboarding must create/update: model-catalog entry, benchmark manifest, quant-profiles entry, and a short README in the model folder describing known failure modes.
- Quarterly review: owners must re-run canonical benchmarks and re-validate quant profiles. If drift is detected (>2% on critical metrics), schedule re-training/mitigation.

Appendix: quick-checklists
- Onboarding quick checklist (tick-box): model metadata | local eval pass | prompt sets created | quant validated | canary plan | security/compliance signoff | Applied ML lead signoff.
- Regression triage contact matrix: model owner -> applied-ml lead -> platform SRE -> product owner -> legal (if data leakage).
